subject: chemistry

items.q: Do all reactions give out heat?
items.correct: No — exothermic reactions release heat, endothermic ones absorb it.
items.misconception: Yes, every reaction releases heat to the surroundings.
items.random_wrong: Energy changes only happen in nuclear reactions.
items.why: Combustion is exothermic; thermal decomposition is endothermic.

items.q: Is breaking chemical bonds exothermic or endothermic?
items.correct: Endothermic — breaking bonds takes in energy.
items.misconception: Exothermic — breaking bonds gives out energy.
items.random_wrong: Bond breaking involves no energy change.
items.why: Breaking bonds requires energy; making bonds releases it. The overall change depends on the balance.

items.q: Does raising the temperature always increase the yield of a reversible reaction?
items.correct: No — it raises the rate, but can lower the yield of an exothermic product.
items.misconception: Yes, higher temperature always means more product.
items.why: Higher temperature speeds reactions, but for an exothermic forward reaction it shifts equilibrium back, lowering yield.
